ai.literal: To think rejoicing and to see gladdening to liquor is not, to love exists.
ai.translation: Merely thinking of it brings intoxication, and seeing it brings joy; this is true of love, but not of liquor.
ai.modern: நினைத்தாலேயே போதை தருவதும், பார்த்தாலேயே மகிழ்ச்சி தருவதும் காதலுக்கு மட்டுமே உண்டு; மதுவுக்கு அந்த இயல்பு இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The couplet contrasts the effects of love with those of intoxicating liquor. Liquor can only intoxicate when it is actually consumed. Love, however, is so powerful that merely thinking about the beloved brings a rush of intoxication, and simply seeing them brings immense joy. The words 'உள்ள' (to think) and 'காண' (to see) highlight how love affects the mind and senses even without physical union.

ai.literal: Even millet-measure not-sulking is needed, even palmyra-measure desire abundantly if comes.
ai.translation: When desire swells as vast as a palmyra tree, one must not sulk even as much as a tiny millet seed.
ai.modern: காமம் பனை மரத்தின் அளவாக நிறைந்து வரும்போது, தினை அளவுகூட ஊடல் கொள்ளாமல் இருக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts two traditional measures of size: the tiny millet seed (தினை) and the massive palmyra tree (பனை). The speaker reflects on the overwhelming nature of her desire for reunion with her lover. When love and desire swell to the immense size of a palmyra tree, there is no room left for feigned anger or lovers' quarrels (ஊடல்). Therefore, she resolves that she must not sulk even a tiny millet's worth, as her vast affection completely overpowers any minor grievances.

ai.literal: Without caring, only desired things even if he does, the husband without seeing they do not rest, the eyes.
ai.translation: Even if my lover disregards me and does only what pleases him, my eyes find no rest without seeing him.
ai.modern: என்னை அன்போடு பேணாமல், தான் விரும்பியவற்றையே என் காதலர் செய்தாலும், அவரைக் காணாமல் என் கண்கள் அமைதி அடைவதில்லை.
ai.explanation: The heroine expresses her uncontrollable eagerness to reunite with her lover. She notes that even if he neglects her and acts only according to his own desires, she cannot maintain her resentment. Her eyes refuse to find peace or rest until they see him, showing how deep love and physical longing override any rational grievance.

ai.literal: Towards sulking I went, alas, O friend; having forgotten that, towards union went my heart.
ai.translation: O friend, I went to him intending to sulk, but my heart forgot that and rushed towards union.
ai.modern: தோழியே, நான் அவரிடம் ஊடல் கொள்ளவே சென்றேன்; ஆனால் என் நெஞ்சம் அதை மறந்து அவருடன் கூடி மகிழவே சென்றுவிட்டது.
ai.explanation: The heroine confides in her close friend about her failure to stay angry with her lover. She explains that she approached him fully intending to engage in feigned anger (ūṭal). However, her heart betrayed her conscious intentions. Forgetting the resolve to sulk, her heart eagerly rushed towards joyful union (kūṭal) instead. This contrast highlights the overpowering nature of her affection, which easily defeats her attempts to be upset.

ai.literal: Painting time stick not-seeing eye-itself like lover's fault I-see-not seen time.
ai.translation: Like the eye that cannot see the kohl-stick when being painted, I cannot see my lover's faults when I look at him.
ai.modern: கண்ணுக்கு மை தீட்டும்போது அந்த மைத்தீட்டும் குச்சியை கண் பார்க்க முடியாதது போல, என் தலைவனை நான் நேரில் பார்க்கும் போது அவனுடைய தவறுகளை என்னால் காண முடிவதில்லை.
ai.explanation: The speaker compares her inability to stay angry at her lover to an eye being painted with kohl. Just as the eye cannot see the stick applying the makeup because it is too close, she cannot see her lover's faults when he is right in front of her. She only remembers his flaws and feels angry when he is away, but his presence blinds her to everything except her love for him.

ai.literal: When seeing, I see not faults that are; when not seeing, I see not things other than fault.
ai.translation: When I see him, I cannot see any of his faults. When I do not see him, I cannot see anything but his faults.
ai.modern: அவரை நேரில் காணும்போது அவருடைய தவறுகள் எதையும் நான் காண்பதில்லை. அவரைக் காணாதபோதோ அவருடைய தவறுகளைத் தவிர வேறு எதையும் நான் காண்பதில்லை.
ai.explanation: The speaker describes the overwhelming nature of her affection and longing. When her lover is present, her joy blinds her to any of his flaws, making him appear perfect. However, when he is away, the pain of separation makes her dwell entirely on his faults, such as his failure to return. The sharp contrast between 'when seeing' (காணுங்கால்) and 'when not seeing' (காணாக்கால்) highlights how her perception is completely dictated by his presence or absence.

ai.literal: Carrying away knowing, water those who leap indeed like; failing knowing, what having sulked?
ai.translation: Like those who leap into a stream knowing it will sweep them away, what is the use of my sulking when I know my resolve will fail?
ai.modern: நீர் தங்களை அடித்துச் செல்லும் என்று அறிந்தும் அதில் குதிப்பவர்களைப் போல, என் ஊடல் தோற்றுப்போகும் என்று தெரிந்தும் நான் ஊடல் கொள்வதால் என்ன பயன்?
ai.explanation: The speaker reflects on the futility of her feigned anger towards her lover. She compares herself to someone who jumps into a fast-flowing stream, fully aware that the current will inevitably sweep them away. Similarly, she knows that her resolve to stay angry will instantly fail ('பொய்த்தல்') the moment she sees him. The couplet beautifully captures the overpowering nature of love, showing that intellectual awareness of one's weakness cannot stop the emotional surrender.

ai.literal: Disgrace-causing unpleasant things even if does, to the intoxicated toddy-like indeed, O thief, your chest.
ai.translation: O thief! Your chest is exactly like toddy to those addicted to it: they desire it even if it causes them disgraceful sorrow.
ai.modern: கள்வா! இழிவான துன்பங்களைச் செய்தாலும், குடித்தவர்களுக்குக் கள் எப்படி விருப்பமானதாக இருக்குமோ, அதுபோலவே உன் மார்பு எனக்கு இருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: The speaker addresses her lover as a 'thief' (கள்வ) because he has stolen her heart and caused her distress by his absence. She compares his chest to toddy (கள்). Toddy brings public disgrace and misery (இளித்தக்க இன்னா) to those who consume it, yet those who are intoxicated by it (களித்தார்க்கு) cannot stay away. In the exact same way, even though her lover's actions have caused her shameful suffering, she remains intoxicated by his love and eagerly desires his embrace.

ai.literal: Even than a flower, it is soft, love; few people its perfect state will experience.
ai.translation: Love is softer than a flower, but only a few ever experience its perfect state.
ai.modern: காதல் மலரை விடவும் மிகவும் மென்மையானது. அதன் சரியான பக்குவத்தை அறிந்து அனுபவிப்பவர்கள் உலகில் சிலரே ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: The couplet compares the nature of love to a flower, stating that love is even softer and more delicate. Because of this extreme delicacy, it requires careful and timely handling to be fully enjoyed. The word cevvi refers to the perfect state or the exact right moment of a flower blooming, which applies here to the delicate timing and understanding needed in love. Only a few people truly grasp this perfect state and experience love completely without bruising it.

ai.literal: With eyes having sulked indeed, she became troubled; embracing, even more than me, she herself eagerness having felt.
ai.translation: She feigned a sulk with her eyes, but quickly became distressed; feeling an eagerness to embrace even greater than mine, she hurried to me.
ai.modern: அவள் தன் கண்களால் மட்டுமே ஊடல் கொண்டு சினந்தாள்; ஆனால் உடனே கலக்கமடைந்து, என்னை விடவும் அதிகமாகத் தழுவிக்கொள்ளும் விருப்பம் கொண்டு விரைந்தாள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet captures a fleeting moment of a lovers' quarrel where the woman attempts to feign anger ('tuṉittē'). However, her anger is entirely superficial, restricted only to her eyes ('kaṇṇiṉ'), and she quickly becomes distressed ('kalaṅkiṉāḷ') at the thought of maintaining the distance. Overcome by an eagerness ('vituppu') for reunion that surpasses even the speaker's own desire ('eṉṉiṉum'), she abandons her pretense and hurries to embrace him. The contrast between her brief, visual sulk and her deep, urgent desire highlights the overpowering nature of their affection.
